title: fix(service-storage, plugin-security): every member can attach files to the records they edit — storage contributes its own attachment set to the member baseline
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu25rjuLxNgaKr1YUx8UMXzr)_

Fixes #32754

## 维护者速读

- 问题：成员能编辑自己的记录，却不能往上面挂附件（403）：没有任何权限集给附件对象授权，附件的行级守门根本轮不到判。
- 改法（按裁定 B）：存储服务自带一个只有「读 + 新建」附件的权限集，经 `everyone` 发给每个登录成员；`member_default` 一字未改（ADR-0090 D9）。安全插件新增一个只在启动期开放的贡献接口来收这个集。
- 条件 ①：四道门（每对象的附件开关、写规则、读可见性、下载的父记录检查）全部装上才贡献；缺任何一道就不发，启动日志点名缺哪道、该补什么。按裁定 A（6841974978），附件开关改由存储服务自己执行，四道门都是存储自己的，每个标志都是安装那一步自己的回答，不再看别的插件的服务名。条件 ②：接口只收贡献者自己登记的对象、只收读和新建，拒通配、其它权限位、行策略、别的包的对象和启动后的调用，每次收下或拒收都记日志，每种拒收各有一条 pin。ADR-0090 那句不在本 PR（另走 Tier H）。
- 条件 ③ 写进 changeset：升级后，已有附件对能读父记录的成员重新可见；成员可以给自己能编辑的记录挂附件；能读不能编辑的成员现在拿到 `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS`（仍是 403）；编辑、删除附件仍要显式授权。外部用户、agent 自身、`fallbackPermissionSet: null` 的部署、不带存储服务的宿主都不变；代成员操作的 agent 受成员和自身 scope 双重约束，成员能挂它才能挂。
- 裁定 A 的升级变化也写进 changeset：之前没挂执行附件开关那个能力的组合上，没声明 `enable.files` 的对象现在对所有人拒绝附件（`FILES_DISABLED`，403），管理员和系统路径也一样，和它的声明（默认关）一致；已经挂在这类对象上的附件保持原样，开关只判新建和改挂。
- 托管运行时每个项目的组合之前有没有挂那个能力：unknown，这个组合不在本仓库里。改了以后它不再影响授权。
- 契约：`ISecurityService` 加一个可选成员 `contributePlatformBaselineSet`（Clause-② widening），不加元数据键，不碰 `docs/adr/`。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

**The grant.** `@objectstack/service-storage` now contributes its own permission set, `storage_attachment_member`: read and create on `sys_attachment`, nothing else. Every signed-in member holds it through the `everyone` anchor, beside `member_default`, as an additive baseline (ADR-0090 D5). `member_default` is unchanged (ADR-0090 D9).

The contribution happens in the storage plugin's `kernel:ready` handler, right after it installs the attachment gates, and only when all four are installed: the per-object opt-in gate (`enable.files`), the write rule, the read-visibility gate and the download door's parent-record check. Each flag is that installation's own answer. A kernel without one of them contributes nothing and says at warn level which gate is missing and what to add, so the object stays refused instead of ungated.

**The opt-in, enforced by the storage service (ruling 6841974978, route A).** `installAttachmentFilesOptInGate` (new, `attachment-files-opt-in.ts`) refuses `403 FILES_DISABLED` on every `sys_attachment` insert, and every update that re-points a row, whose target object does not declare `enable: { files: true }`. An unregistered object or an unreadable definition is refused too. It runs for every caller, the system path included, and reads the live definition on each write. It is installed first, before the write rule, so every gate the grant relies on is the storage service's own, and no other plugin's order is involved. Another gate that enforces the same declaration may also run; both read the one definition and refuse with the one code.

**Whether the hosted runtime mounted the capability that enforced the opt-in before: unknown.** The hosted runtime's per-project composition is not in this repository, and nothing here composes that capability for a host kernel. Measured on head `e8eb97dc`, `objectstack dev` on `examples/app-todo` does compose it, and a member there was granted. With this change the answer no longer decides either the grant or the opt-in.

An agent principal gains nothing in its own right. An agent acting for a member is bounded by that member and by its own scope (ADR-0090 D10), so it can attach where the member can, within that scope.

**The seam.** `ISecurityService` gains an optional member, `contributePlatformBaselineSet(contributor, set)`. `SecurityPlugin` implements it with `PlatformBaselineSets`. Its rules:

- It is open only during boot. The window closes at `kernel:bootstrapped`.
- Each contributor gives one set, and the set carries only the closed keys.
- The set names only objects that the engine registry holds under the contributor's package.
- Each object entry carries only `allowRead` and `allowCreate`.

An admitted set is registered in the catalog under the contributor's package. When the deployment declares a member baseline, the set's name joins the one composed baseline array that every baseline reader shares: the data plane, explain, effective access, the describe fallback and the `everyone` definition. A set that joins after the `kernel:ready` derivation has begun causes one re-derivation of the anchor at `kernel:bootstrapped`. Every admission and every refusal is logged.

**Docs.**

- `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx` gains a "Who holds the object grant" section. Its callout and its enforcement summary now say that the baseline grants read and create, and that edit and delete need an explicit grant. Its opt-in section says the storage service enforces the opt-in on insert and re-point, for every caller, wherever it runs.
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`: a note under the built-in sets table that a platform service can contribute a baseline set of its own, and that the storage service contributes `storage_attachment_member`.
- The stale header of `attachment-access-hooks.ts` is fixed.

**Error-code ledger.** `FILES_DISABLED` is listed under `@objectstack/service-storage` as a second emitter of a code another package already registers: provenance, not a new code.

## Tests

| Ruling item | Pin |
|---|---|
| The grant lands only with all four gates installed; no middleware means no grant | `storage-service-plugin.test.ts` (the order: opt-in gate, write rule, read visibility, then the grant; no middleware seam, no auth service, no hook seam: each contributes nothing and the warning names the gate); `attachment-member-grant.test.ts` (each missing gate, with the remedy named; no security service, no seam, a refusing seam, no baseline) |
| The flag is the gate, not a service name | `storage-service-plugin.test.ts`: a kernel with no other opt-in capability gets the grant, and the opt-in still refuses on insert and re-point; a kernel with a service registered under that capability's name, on an engine without the hook seam, gets no grant and the warning names the opt-in gate. `attachment-files-opt-in.test.ts`: installed answers `true` only when both registrations went through |
| The opt-in, enforced by the storage service | `attachment-files-opt-in.test.ts`: `files: false`, no `files`, no enable block, an unregistered object, an unreadable or absent definition all refuse; `files: true` admits; the system context is not exempt; a write naming no parent object passes; the live definition is read on each write |
| Each seam refusal | `platform-baseline-sets.test.ts`: unnamed contributor, closed window, row policy, every non-closed key, a second set, another contributor's name or a shipped name, no registry, no object, `'*'`, another package's object, an unregistered object, every bit other than read and create (even when `false`), non-boolean values, an entry that grants nothing, a malformed set, the registry refusing |
| Seam on a real kernel | `platform-baseline-sets.integration.test.ts`: a member reads and creates, and cannot edit or delete; explain names the set as an additive baseline; the `everyone` definition names it even though it landed after the derivation; the catalog holds it under the service's package; an external user gets nothing; an agent principal's own leg gets nothing; another package's object is refused on the real registry; the window is closed after bootstrap; `fallbackPermissionSet: null` admits the set and hands it to no one |
| Every contribution logged | same file: the admission line (set, contributor, grants, joined), the refusal line at warn (contributor, reason), and the no-baseline admission line |
| Upload-complete `attachTo` and the MCP `create_upload_link` door; an agent acting for the member on an OAuth token (admitted where the member and the token's scope both allow; refused with the attach rule's code where the member does not; the same call on a read-only token refused at the door, minting nothing); `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS` on a readable-but-not-editable record; unreadable records' attachments stay invisible (list, total, by id); another user's attachment on a readable record is visible; `FILES_DISABLED`; explain names the storage set; a host without the storage service still answers 403 with no storage set; the storage service and the security plugin alone hand the grant out, and the opt-in refuses there for the member, the administrator and a system-path re-point | `member-attachment-baseline.dogfood.test.ts` (new, real stack, 13 tests) |
| Contract | `security-service.test.ts` (the member is optional, and its type carries only read and create); `registered-security-service-members.pin.test.ts` |

Four existing expectations move with the change:

- `security-catalog-showcase`: the permission catalog lists `storage_attachment_member` in every showcase posture. The security service registers an admitted platform baseline set in the catalog under the contributing package, so the catalog read and the metadata door both list it, and it resolves by name; it is the set the `everyone` definition and explain name. The expected names add it as its producer names it, not read off a registry.

- `showcase-d7-default-profile` now lists the storage set on the `everyone` definition: the harness composes the storage service, and every gate is its own.
- `print-service-archive`: an auditor who can read but not edit the invoice is now refused by the attach rule (`ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS`) instead of by the missing object grant. It is still a 403, and still raised before any mint or render.
- `catalog-reference-report` now sees two `kernel:bootstrapped` handlers, and the report is still the last.

**After the merge-queue ejection** (head `3ec4b7b3`): the queue's full Dogfood Regression Gate found `security-catalog-showcase` expecting the catalog without the storage set (above). That expectation moved (`84c30f2b`, one test file), and `main` was merged again before re-entering the queue (merge commit `3ec4b7b3`, 17 commits, no conflict):

- `@objectstack/service-storage` full: 81 files, 1512 passed. `@objectstack/plugin-security`, the four suites this PR touches: 72 passed. `@objectstack/spec` `security-service.test.ts` and `error-code-ledger.test.ts`: 56 passed.
- The WHOLE dogfood battery, not only the affected suites: 461 files, 458 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (3856 tests passed, 42 skipped). The same battery on `84c30f2b` before the merge: 458 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` over the PR's change set on the merged tree: 130 derived, 130 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, every exit 0. On `84c30f2b`, the gates the changed test file derives: 52 run, every exit 0.

**After the pre-queue merge of `main`** (merge commit `1b46bf82`, 56 commits, no conflict; head `b9878efd`, which also adds one changeset sentence: attachments already stored on an object without the opt-in stay as they are, since the opt-in judges only a new attachment and a re-point):

- `@objectstack/service-storage` full: 81 files, 1512 passed. `@objectstack/plugin-security`, the four suites this PR touches: 72 passed. `@objectstack/spec` `security-service.test.ts` and `error-code-ledger.test.ts`: 56 passed.
- Dogfood on the merged tree (dependency `dist` rebuilt): the affected suites, 57 files, 56 green and 1 skipped as on `main`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` over the PR's change set on the merged tree: 130 derived, 130 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, every exit 0.

At head `4b9e6ad1` (ruling A on top of `e8eb97dc`; merge-base then `5fb79bc0`). Only the gates and suites that round touched were run again.

- Unit suites: `@objectstack/service-storage` (full: 80 files, 1499 passed, before the last one-line change to the branch without the hook seam; the three suites it touches, 54 passed after it). Typechecks for service-storage (source and test projects) and dogfood. ESLint on the changed files is clean. `@objectstack/spec` gains only the ledger row: its ledger suites (26 passed), `check:error-code-provenance` and `check:generated` are green. plugin-security is untouched this round (its runs are in the round-1 record below).
- Dogfood (real stack): the new suite (13 tests) plus the suites that touch attachments, explain, the `everyone` anchor or the storage service, 54 files: 53 green and one expectation that moves (`showcase-d7-default-profile`, above), then green.
- Ablations this round. Each one reverts one guard, turns its pin red, and is then restored, with the blob equal to `HEAD` and a clean tree:
  - the opt-in refusal (`attachment-files-opt-in.test.ts` and the storage plugin pins red);
  - the fourth flag read from a service name instead of the installation (the grant goes missing where no other opt-in capability is composed);
  - the name lookup in the branch without the hook seam (the "name counts for nothing" pin);
  - the installer's answer when the hook seam is missing, and when a registration is refused;
  - the opt-in gate installed after the grant instead of first (the order pin);
  - the warning's remedy sentence;
  - on the built artifact (`dist` rebuilt, the marker proved present, then proved absent after the restore): with the opt-in refusal disabled, the storage-alone host's two opt-in tests go red, and the main suite's own opt-in test stays green as the control, since another opt-in gate is composed there; with the fourth flag read from a service name, the storage-alone host loses the grant and goes red.
  - The read-only token pin holds under one ablation of the MCP tool registration: with the tool offered on a read-only token, the call is still refused, now `PERMISSION_DENIED` by the token's scope ceiling at the data plane. The scope limb is defended twice, and the pin asserts the refused call, not the menu.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` over the gates this round's paths derive: 129 derived, 129 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, every exit 0 (one first-run red, `check:error-code-provenance`, fixed by the ledger row above and rerun with every gate the two late paths derive). `check:generated` for spec is current.

Round 1 (head `e8eb97dc`; plugin-security unchanged since): plugin-security full 266 files, 6573 passed at the round-0 head, and the four suites round 1 touched, 72 passed; spec `security-service.test.ts` 30 passed; `check:generated` current; the seam ablations (owner check, bit allowlist, wildcard, row policy, window close, log lines, re-derivation, null-baseline join) red then restored; 128 gates, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
